claims.text: The target material is a multi-component, Ta-based refractory BCC high-entropy alloy in the solid state near melting.
Standard experimental measurements of melting properties are infeasible for the target alloy.
Full DFT thermodynamic integration over the relevant phase space is prohibitively expensive.
A free-energy perturbation scheme using an MLP can bypass full thermodynamic integration.
The MLP must cover both solid and liquid configurations of the specific Ta-based alloy.
High-temperature liquid configurations are required in the training set to prevent collapse toward solid-state minima during perturbation.
The perturbation calculation should be applied near the solidus/liquidus transition.
Liquid short-range order and coordination numbers are important structural mediators of the free-energy prediction.
Standard EAM potentials often fail to reproduce the complex liquid structure of multi-component refractory alloys.
A liquid-enriched MLP can learn complex many-body liquid interactions that empirical potentials miss.
Learning the liquid many-body interactions enables accurate estimation of the solid-liquid free-energy difference without full thermodynamic integration.
ML methods can provide computationally inexpensive predictions in high-entropy-alloy applications.
The proposed MLP can evaluate energies and forces faster than DFT.
The proposed MLP can retain DFT-comparable accuracy for liquid structure.
The liquid-enriched MLP perturbation method will predict melting temperature and free-energy differences within 5% of a small-scale DFT thermodynamic-integration benchmark.
Standard EAM perturbation will produce an incorrect liquid structure and erroneous free-energy differences.
The liquid-enriched MLP perturbation method will reduce computational cost by an order of magnitude relative to full DFT thermodynamic integration.
The approach is applicable to multi-component refractory BCC alloys exhibiting liquid phase separation or complex short-range order.
Insufficiently diverse liquid training data can cause the proposed method to fail.
Extrapolation into phase-space regions absent from the training data can cause the proposed method to fail.
